title: Finite etale splitting of generic components of a finite type family
statement: Let $T$ be an integral Noetherian scheme [def-pc-integral-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth], where Noetherian means locally Noetherian and quasi-compact, let $f:X\to T$ be a finite type morphism [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and use scheme-theoretic fibres [def-pc-scheme-fibre]. There exist a nonempty affine open $U\subseteq T$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], an integral affine scheme $S$, and a finite etale surjective morphism $\pi:S\to U$ [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism, def-weil-etale-morphism, def-weil-surjective-morphism] such that, writing $\xi$ for the generic point of $S$ [def-sc-generic-point], every irreducible component of $(X\times_T S)_\xi$ [def-pc-fibre-product, def-weil-irreducible-components] is geometrically irreducible over $\kappa(\xi)$ [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible, def-weil-residue-field]. Geometric irreducibility means that its inverse image is irreducible and nonempty after every field extension. No properness, flatness, reducedness or dimension assumption on $X/T$ is imposed; the generic fibre may be empty.

source.place: Tag 0551 (lemma-make-components-generic-fibre-geometrically-irreducible), statement and proof, lines 6771--6830; integral Noetherian base specialization of the irreducible affine cover, whose reducedness follows from etale.tex Proposition 025O (proposition-etale-reduced).

proof.text: Choose a point of the nonempty scheme $T$ and an affine open neighbourhood $V=\operatorname{Spec}A$ using [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis]. The ring $A$ is Noetherian by [pqf-lem-affine-open-locnoeth], since $T$ is locally Noetherian, and is a domain by [def-pc-integral-scheme], since $V$ is nonempty. Put $K=\operatorname{Frac}(A)$ and use the canonical morphism $\operatorname{Spec}K\to V\to T$. Write $Y=X\times_T\operatorname{Spec}K$. The finite-type base-change assertion of [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change] makes $Y\to\operatorname{Spec}K$ finite type. In particular this step does not assume that $X\to T$ is flat or dominant.

source.place: Tag 0551 (lemma-make-components-generic-fibre-geometrically-irreducible), choosing an affine open and passing to the generic field; morphisms.tex Tag 01T4

proof.text: Apply [lem-sbc-generic-components-split] to $Y/K$. It gives a field extension $L/K$ whose spectrum map is finite etale and for which every irreducible component of $G=Y\times_K\operatorname{Spec}L$ has irreducible nonempty inverse image after every field extension of $L$. Finiteness of this spectrum map means that $L$ is a finite $K$-module, by [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] applied to the whole affine target. The two spectra have one point with residue fields $L$ and $K$; apply [lem-weil-pbc-etale-residue-field-extension-separable] at that point. Thus this very extension $L/K$ is finite-dimensional and separable algebraic, as required by the spreading theorem.

source.place: Tag 054R (lemma-finite-extension-geometrically-irreducible-components); the field extension used in more-morphisms.tex Tag 0551

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-spread-finite-separable-extension] to the Noetherian domain $A$, its fraction field $K$, and the finite separable extension $L/K$ just obtained. We obtain $c\in A$, $c\ne0$, and a finite etale $A[c^{-1}]$-algebra $B$ which is a domain with fraction field $L$, together with the finite etale surjective spectrum map $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}A[c^{-1}]$. The fraction-field identification is over $K$, so the composite $A\to A[c^{-1}]\to B\to L$ is the original map $A\to K\to L$. These are exactly the field extension and the compatible model needed below; no normality of $A$ is required.

source.place: Tag 0551 (lemma-make-components-generic-fibre-geometrically-irreducible), spreading the separable extension by a monic polynomial and shrinking to its etale locus; the same calculation in literature/blueprint/master/blueprint/sec-smooth-purity/sk-prop-sf-cbc/lem-weil-pbc-finite-pushforward-generic-constructible.md

proof.text: Let $U=D(c)\subseteq V$. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-localization-away-basic-open], $\operatorname{Spec}A[c^{-1}]\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is a homeomorphism onto this open; $U$ is nonempty because it contains $(0)$. This is also an isomorphism onto the open subscheme $U$: the affine stalk descriptions of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization] identify its stalk map over a prime $\mathfrak p$ not containing $c$ with $A_{\mathfrak p}\to(A[c^{-1}])_{\mathfrak p A[c^{-1}]}$. The inverse sends $(a/c^n)/(b/c^m)$ to $ac^m/(bc^n)$; the denominators are outside $\mathfrak p$. For a section on the target sheaf, lift each germ locally using stalk surjectivity; injectivity makes these lifts agree after shrinking on overlaps, so the sheaf axiom glues them to a unique preimage. Thus the sheaf map is an isomorphism and the schemes are identified. Set $S=\operatorname{Spec}B$ and transport the model map to $\pi:S\to U$. The preceding step supplies finiteness, etaleness and surjectivity, and $U$ is an affine open of $T$.

source.place: Tag 01HV (lemma-spec-sheaves), affine stalks; algebra.tex Tag 00E4 (lemma-standard-open); elementary localization calculation identifying the affine open in Tag 0551

proof.text: The nonempty open $U$ is integral by [def-pc-integral-scheme]: every nonempty affine open in it is such an open in $T$ and therefore has a domain coordinate ring. In particular $U$ is reduced. Since $\pi$ is etale, [etale-proposition-etale-reduced] implies that $S$ is reduced. The prime $(0)\subset B$ is a point $\xi$ with closure $V((0))=\operatorname{Spec}B$, by the Zariski topology and the fact that $B$ is a domain. Thus $S$ is irreducible and nonempty, and is integral by the reduced-and-irreducible characterization in [def-pc-integral-scheme]. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization] its local ring at $\xi$ is $B_{(0)}=\operatorname{Frac}(B)=L$: every nonzero element of $B$ is inverted. This is a field with maximal ideal zero, so [def-weil-residue-field] gives $\kappa(\xi)=L$, compatibly with $A\to K\to L$.

source.place: Tag 025O (proposition-etale-reduced), applied to the cover of Tag 0551; schemes.tex Tag 01HV and elementary generic-point calculation for a domain

proof.text: By [def-pc-scheme-fibre], the fibre to be considered is $H=(X\times_T S)\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(\xi)$. Under $\kappa(\xi)=L$, the morphism $\operatorname{Spec}L\to S\to T$ equals the morphism through $\operatorname{Spec}K$. Apply the universal property [def-pc-fibre-product] twice: both $H$ and $G=(X\times_T\operatorname{Spec}K)\times_K\operatorname{Spec}L$ represent pairs of maps to $X$ and $\operatorname{Spec}L$ agreeing in $T$. The comparison maps preserving these projections are inverse, since their composites preserve both projections. This is an isomorphism over $L$. For any extension $E/L$, its pullback is likewise an isomorphism preserving the projections to $H$ and $G$. An isomorphism is a homeomorphism, so it takes maximal irreducible subsets to maximal irreducible subsets, by [def-weil-irreducible-components]. The inverse image of each such subset in the $E$-fibre is identified with the corresponding inverse image for $G$. Step 2 says the latter is irreducible and nonempty for every $E$. This proves the required geometric irreducibility. If $Y$ is empty the same pullback identities give $G=H=\varnothing$, and the assertion about every component is vacuous; the chosen $S$ and $U$ remain nonempty.

lean.statement: theorem exists_finite_etale_generic_component_splitting {X T : Scheme.{u}} [IsIntegral T] [IsLocallyNoetherian T] [CompactSpace T] (f : X ⟶ T) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f] : ∃ U : T.Opens, (U : Set T).Nonempty ∧ IsAffineOpen U ∧ ∃ S : Scheme.{u}, IsIntegral S ∧ IsAffine S ∧ ∃ π : S ⟶ U.toScheme, IsFinite π ∧ Etale π ∧ Surjective π ∧ ∃ ξ : S, IsGenericPoint ξ Set.univ ∧ ∀ A ∈ irreducibleComponents ↥((pullback.snd f (π ≫ U.ι)).fiber ξ), ∀ (E : Type u) (_ : Field E) (z : Spec (CommRingCat.of E) ⟶ Spec (S.residueField ξ)), IsIrreducible ((pullback.fst ((pullback.snd f (π ≫ U.ι)).fiberToSpecResidueField ξ) z) ⁻¹' A)
